This time, the number of colors suggested by k d + 1 k_{d}+1 is smaller than the bound on the chromatic number given by Brooks’s theorem, so we used k d + 1 = 4 k_{d}+1=4 colors in the algorithm. The results are recorded in Figure 9 . The algorithm performed extremely well with 4 4 colors, and it performed perfectly when we increased the number of colors to 5 5 . Thus, in both cases, the algorithm was perfectly able to find proper r r -colorings of r r -regular graphs. For 6 6 -regular graphs with 4 4 colors, the algorithm’s performance was significantly better than its performance on Erdős-Rényi graphs of the same order and average degree. This suggests that either the uniform degree sequence or some other resulting property of regular graphs makes it easier for the algorithm to find a proper coloring.
